title: Productivity suite users, sign-in and MFA settings
source_system: Productivity suite admin console (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Business plan, basic tier; one user account, the owner's, which is also the administrator account; the day helpers have no accounts; MFA is on with text-message codes sent to the owner's phone; the phone is the only registered second factor and no backup codes have been generated; email is the recovery address for the owner's other service accounts; the sign-in activity list and new-device alert emails are available to the administrator

title: Productivity suite file storage, sharing and version settings review
source_system: Productivity suite admin console and file storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Folders hold daily gauge sheets, run ticket copies, a synced program folder with PLC and RTU program copies in per-customer subfolders for Customers A and B, customer network notes, MSAs and insurance certificates, training certificates, and scanned W-9 forms for the 2 helpers (both with Florida addresses); file version history is kept 30 days (plan default); no other backup or retention setting is configured; the program copies carry no record of which version was loaded to which controller

title: Accounting service users and sign-in settings
source_system: Accounting service settings (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: One user account, the owner's, which is the administrator account; password sign-in; MFA is available and turned off; the bank feed is connected; contractor records for the 2 helpers hold their names and Social Security numbers for 1099 reporting; customer billing contacts for the 4 customers; a sign-in activity list is available

title: Sales by customer and service line, 2025, and June 2026 invoices
source_system: Accounting service reports (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: 2025 receipts of about $180,000: contract pumping about $115,000 and automation service about $65,000; Customer A about 45% of receipts; about $15,000 invoiced a month on 30-day terms; all 4 customers pay by ACH; June 2026 pumping invoices bill 34 wells (Customer A 18, Customer B 6, Customer C 6, Customer D 4); automation service is invoiced to Customers A and B only, with line items for program and setpoint change jobs

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the tax preparer)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; contract labor paid to 2 day helpers on Form 1099-NEC; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees; principal business code 213112

title: Field laptop settings and installed software review
source_system: Field laptop settings screens (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One local account, an administrator, used for email, web browsing and control work; installed: email and web browser, PLC, RTU and flow meter configuration software (licensed per device), the Customer A VPN client, the Customer B remote-desktop client, an attended remote-support app (session started by the owner), and the file sync client for SYS-01; full-disk encryption on; automatic OS updates on and update history current; built-in antivirus on with real-time protection and automatic updates; host firewall on; screen lock after 5 minutes; no backup configured other than the sync client; a spreadsheet of customer site passwords is stored on the laptop

title: Smartphone settings and apps review
source_system: Smartphone settings screens (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: Passcode and fingerprint unlock; device encryption on with the passcode; screen lock after 1 minute; automatic updates on; remote locate and wipe not set up; used for business and personal purposes; holds business email, the text-message MFA codes for SYS-01, the hotspot used by the laptop, the Customer A alarm viewer app (view only), photos of gauges and run tickets, and a free generative AI chatbot app

title: USB drives and programming cables review
source_system: Owner equipment (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: 3 USB drives, none encrypted; one drive holds personal files and customer program files together; the drives hold program copies from earlier jobs; serial and Ethernet programming cables kept with the laptop for well-site use

title: Home internet account and connected-device list
source_system: Internet service provider account app (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: Router supplied by the internet service provider; one Wi-Fi network; the connected-device list shows the field laptop, the phone, and family members' phones, tablets and TV on the same network

title: Customer A MSA and security schedule (2025 renewal)
source_system: Signed agreements folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Work scope: contract pumping and well-site automation service at Customer A's onshore production facilities in the Florida Panhandle; security schedule items (1) protect Customer A confidential information, never in personal accounts, (2) remote access only through Customer A's VPN with Customer A-issued MFA, (3) notice to the production superintendent within 24 hours of discovery of a suspected security incident, (4) no logic or setpoint change without the production superintendent's written (email) approval and a record of each change, (5) no disclosure to third parties, including software services, without written consent, (6) return or destroy data within 30 days after the MSA ends, (7) annual security questionnaire organized by NIST CSF 2.0, (8) technology errors and omissions or cyber liability coverage of at least $1 million while holding remote access; general liability and commercial auto certificates required

title: MSAs for Customers B, C and D
source_system: Signed agreements folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Work scope: contract pumping (all three) and well-site automation service (Customer B) at onshore production facilities and flow lines; each has a standard confidentiality clause (customer information is confidential and is returned on request); none has a security schedule, remote access terms, or incident notice terms; general liability and commercial auto certificates required

title: Customer A VPN account letter and VPN client profile
source_system: Signed agreements folder (SYS-01); VPN client on the field laptop (SYS-03)
owner: Customer A IT and SCADA contact
what_it_shows: Customer A's IT and SCADA contact issued a named VPN account and a Customer A MFA token to the owner after confirming the owner's identity; the letter describes the VPN gateway, the sign-in steps and the contact for access problems; the VPN client profile on the laptop requires the Customer A token at sign-in

title: Customer B remote-desktop access emails
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Customer B's operations manager emailed, after a phone call, the shared login for a third-party remote-desktop tool on Customer B's SCADA operator workstation; the email says Customer B's own staff use the same login and the tool is left on for unattended access; sign-in is by password with no second factor; no agreement or remote access terms are attached; the tool's published documentation states that sessions are encrypted; the inbox holds no later message from the owner to Customer B about the login

title: Inbox and file search: Customer A change approvals and change records
source_system: Email inbox and file storage (SYS-01); field laptop (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: The inbox holds email approvals from the Customer A production superintendent for some logic and setpoint changes; no change log, change request form, or record of changes made on customer controllers was found in SYS-01 or on the laptop

title: Customer A 2026 security questionnaire request
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
owner: Customer A IT and SCADA contact
what_it_shows: Customer A's IT and SCADA contact sent the 2026 annual security questionnaire, organized by NIST CSF 2.0, with answers due 2026-09-30

title: Customer site orientation packets (Customers A to D)
source_system: File storage (SYS-01); copies from each customer
what_it_shows: Site packets for the onshore leases in the Florida Panhandle, within about 60 miles of the owner's home; tank batteries have hardwired high-level switches that shut in the wells, wired at the site and not connected to the owner's laptop, phone or accounts; each customer shuts in its wells before a hurricane; site contacts and emergency numbers for each customer

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-12
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the productivity suite provider, the accounting service provider, the phone carrier, the internet service provider, the configuration software makers (annual licenses), and the general liability and commercial auto insurer; per-well payments to the dynamometer analysis service from March 2026; hourly payments to the IT technician; payments to the 2 day helpers; ACH receipts from the 4 customers; no payment for cyber or technology errors and omissions coverage; no payment to an AI chatbot service

title: Insurance declarations and certificates of insurance
source_system: Insurance agent portal; file storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: General liability and commercial auto policies in force for 2026; certificates of insurance issued to Customers A to D as the MSAs require; no cyber liability or technology errors and omissions coverage is listed

title: IT technician invoices, 2024-03-01 to 2026-06-30
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Hourly invoices for laptop, phone and home network help; the 2024 laptop setup invoice lists full-disk encryption turned on and the configuration software installed; later invoices describe attended remote-support sessions started by the owner

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Field laptop; file storage (SYS-01); email inbox; paper files in the home office
what_it_shows: No written security policy or procedure was found, including a risk assessment, incident plan, contact list for security events, backup procedure, change log, data or software inventory, list of customer field devices or credentials, list of service providers and the data each holds, remote session log, or end-of-contract data return procedure; no written coverage agreement with the nearby contract pumper was found

title: Training certificates
source_system: File storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Oilfield safety certificates required by the MSAs (H2S awareness, first aid and CPR, defensive driving); no cybersecurity or OT security course appears

title: Dynamometer analysis service account, subscription and settings
source_system: Dynamometer analysis service (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Subscription since March 2026, priced per well; 14 rod-pumped wells for Customers A and B uploaded under lease and well names; dynamometer cards and run times uploaded by the owner; password sign-in, with MFA offered on the paid tier only; the automatic optimization feature that can push setpoints to pump controllers is shown as off, and the account history shows no setpoint pushes

title: Dynamometer analysis service terms and pricing, as accepted
source_system: Dynamometer service provider website
what_it_shows: Standard terms let the provider use uploaded data to improve its models; the pricing page lists a paid tier with a no-training option and MFA, which at the current 14 wells costs about $300 a year more

title: Inbox and file search for customer consent to third-party services
source_system: Email inbox and file storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: No written consent from Customer A or Customer B to upload their data to the dynamometer service or any other software service was found; no message to any customer about the uploads

title: Generative AI chatbot account history
source_system: Free generative AI chatbot account (phone app)
what_it_shows: Free tier; chat history on; about 12 chats from April to July 2026 in which well names and daily production numbers for Customers A and C were pasted to draft monthly service summaries; the terms allow the provider to use inputs to improve the service

title: Daily gauge sheets and paper gauge book, June 2026
source_system: Email sent folder (SYS-01); paper gauge book
what_it_shows: The paper gauge book carried on rounds holds the day's tank gauges and well checks; a daily gauge sheet is emailed to each of the 4 customers; run ticket copies and phone photos of gauges are filed in SYS-01

title: Insurance agent's cyber liability estimate
source_system: Email from the insurance agent (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Answer to the intake request of 2026-07-15: estimate of about $1,300 a year for cyber liability coverage of $1 million; the current general liability and commercial auto policies do not cover cyber events

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner-operator's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT technician
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the systems and providers used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; customers expect daily gauges by 9 a.m.; the owner is the only person who performs each function; the nearby contract pumper covers rounds informally when either is sick or away; the owner programs about 60 field devices for Customers A and B; the IT technician estimates about one working day to move the licensed configuration software, with license transfer, to a replacement laptop

title: Risk walkthrough of the laptop, phone, truck, home office and SaaS accounts
source_system: Walkthrough with the IT technician, 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-22
what_it_shows: The laptop stays in the locked truck at well sites and is sometimes left visible on the seat; the home office door locks; the router admin page opened with the maker's default password; family devices share the Wi-Fi; on 2026-07-22 the file listing showed the customer password spreadsheet in the SYS-01 synced folder, with its file versions; customer program copies are on the laptop and in the synced folder only; email is the reset path for the other accounts

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner-operator's written answers to the CSF 2.0 and SP 800-82 Rev. 3 questions, checked on screen with the IT technician
what_it_shows: The owner had not read Customer A's security schedule closely before July 2026 and did not know the 24-hour notice clause or that the business is a covered entity under Fla. Stat. 501.171; Customers B, C and D were never asked about security expectations; 23 logic or setpoint changes were made for Customer A in the last 12 months (from invoices and job notes), 4 with email approval and the rest approved by phone; USB drives are not scanned before use on customer equipment; family members used the laptop for web browsing and installed browser add-ons; configuration software and firmware are downloaded from makers' sites without checksum checks and updated only when a device needs it; sign-in lists were never reviewed and new-device emails were not acted on; the home network is not monitored; no threat information is received; the dynamometer service and the chatbot were adopted without reading their terms; no exercises or lessons-learned practice; hurricane steps are informal; the router is several years old; insurance and MSA renewals are decided without a risk review

title: Productivity suite provider SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: Provider trust portal (downloaded by the owner)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security, Availability and Confidentiality categories for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31; unqualified opinion; one Availability exception (an unmonitored backup job), remediated; lists complementary user entity controls (manage users and MFA, configure sharing and retention, review sign-in activity, protect endpoints and credentials); describes encryption of stored files and redundant storage

title: Owner's email to Customer B on remote access
source_system: Email sent folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Sent 2026-07-24 to Customer B's operations manager: asks for named accounts, MFA, and access turned on only for scheduled sessions on the remote-desktop tool

title: Control assessment: MFA on privileged accounts
source_system: Account security pages of SYS-01 and SYS-02; laptop sign-in; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Email administrator account required a text-message code; the accounting service administrator account and the laptop administrator account signed in with a password only

title: Control assessment: MFA on non-privileged accounts
source_system: Account security pages of SYS-01 and SYS-08; Customer A VPN sign-in; sign-in tests
what_it_shows: Email and the Customer A VPN required a second factor; the dynamometer service signed in with a password only; the Customer B path has no MFA (customer-controlled)

title: Control assessment: non-privileged account test
source_system: Laptop account settings; test install from the daily account
what_it_shows: The only laptop account is an administrator used for email, web browsing and control work; a test install ran without any prompt for separate credentials

title: Control assessment: authenticator management review
source_system: Password spreadsheet (reviewed on screen, not copied); remote client settings; router settings; settings of 6 customer field devices viewed with each customer's permission during routine site visits on 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-23; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The owner is the only user of every account; Customer A verified the owner before issuing the VPN token; customer passwords sit in a plain spreadsheet synced to the file account; the Customer B remote-desktop client stored the shared password, and the owner removed it during the session on 2026-07-23; the Customer B shared password has not changed since 2024 and Customer B staff use the same login; the home router admin password and several of the sampled modem and controller passwords are the maker defaults; password strength is mixed and some passwords are reused across customer devices; no procedure for a lost phone or an exposed customer password; laptop disk and phone encrypted and screens lock

title: Control assessment: information exchange agreements review
source_system: MSAs for Customers A to D; Customer A security schedule and VPN account letter; Customer B emails; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Customer A exchange is managed under its security schedule, with the VPN interface documented in its account letter and controls and responsibilities named; the Customer B remote path was set up by phone with no agreement and the remote tool is not documented; security requirements, controls and responsibilities are written for Customer A only; no personal information is exchanged and all four MSAs have confidentiality terms; no agreement states the impact level of the information; no review cycle for the agreements

title: Control assessment: backup review and restore test
source_system: Synced folder and file version settings; laptop storage review; provider SOC 2 report; restore of one program file
what_it_shows: Customer program copies exist only on the laptop and the synced folder, with no offline copy; no backup of the laptop configuration or licensed software setup; security documents and change notes are kept only in the file account with 30-day versions; the provider encrypts stored files and versions and stores them redundantly (SOC 2 report); no hashes or checks on copies; a 20-day-old version of one program file was restored in the test

title: Control assessment: change control review
source_system: Customer A approval emails; program files on the laptop; owner self-review of the last 12 months of changes
what_it_shows: No written list of which changes need approval; changes discussed by phone with no record of review; 4 of 23 Customer A changes had email approval and 19 were approved by phone only; the 4 email-approved changes matched the program files loaded (compared 2026-07-23); no change records retained; no monitoring or later review of changes; the customer approver is named only in Customer A's MSA

title: Control assessment: USB drive review
source_system: The 3 USB drives; scan history on the laptop; owner self-review
what_it_shows: One drive holds personal files and customer programs; the laptop scan history shows no drive scanned before use on customer equipment; all 3 drives belong to the owner and drives of unknown origin are not used

title: Control assessment: malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus status page; standard antivirus test file downloaded and copied to a USB drive
what_it_shows: The built-in antivirus detected the test file on download and when copied from the USB drive and quarantined it; signature updates install automatically (last update the same day); daily scheduled quick scan and real-time protection on; the alert was shown to the owner; no false positives recorded

title: Control assessment: incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contact lists; Customer A MSA clause (3); owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time is defined; the owner did not know the 24-hour Customer A clause; there is no list of whom to notify (customers, IT technician, counsel, insurer)
